# Collected powerups need some feel

## Headline

Add tactile collection feedback: a new short "pop" SFX plus a generic
"sucked into the ship" absorb VFX that plays whenever a power-up drop is
collected.

## Problem statement

Collecting a power-up currently gives almost no feedback. In every collection
path the drop's `Graphics` object is destroyed on the same frame and, in most
paths, a generic two-tone chime (`playPowerUpCollectSound()`) plays. There is no
visual confirmation of the pickup and no distinct "pop" sound, so collection
lacks the tactile, satisfying "feel" expected of an arcade shooter.

## Users

- **Players** — want collecting a power-up to feel satisfying and clearly
  confirmed through sound and motion.
- **Playtesters / designers** — want consistent, observable collection feedback
  across the main game and the gym scenes so the behaviour can be judged and
  tuned in one place.

### Example user stories

- As a player, when my ship flies over a power-up I want to see it get sucked
  into my ship and hear a satisfying pop, so that collecting feels rewarding.
- As a developer, I want the collection feedback implemented once in a shared
  helper and reused by every scene, so the game and the gyms never diverge.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Pop SFX:** A new collection "pop" sound is added to
  `src/audio/effects.ts` (Web Audio synthesis, matching the existing
  best-effort/no-op-without-`AudioContext` pattern). It is short and
  percussive, and audibly distinct from the existing
  `playPowerUpCollectSound()` chime. It is played whenever a power-up drop is
  collected. A unit test asserts the function exists and safely no-ops without
  an audio context.
- [ ] **AC2 — Absorb VFX:** On collection a drop visibly performs a "suck into
  the ship" animation: its position converges on the player ship, its scale
  shrinks toward zero, and its shape/shear morphs as it is drawn in. The
  animation completes in a short, tunable duration (target ≤ 0.3 s) and then the
  `Graphics` object is destroyed. The ship's world position is the attractor. A
  single generic absorb treatment is used for all drop types (power-ups and
  weapon drops); no per-type VFX variants.
- [ ] **AC3 — Shared implementation:** The absorb animation is implemented once
  as a reusable helper (pure update + thin Phaser-facing entry point, mirroring
  `src/powerups/magnet.ts` / `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`) and used by every
  power-up collection path — `PlayScene`, the shared `GymFormationScene` base
  (covering `GymEnemies`/`GymBoss`), and the legacy `GymPowerUps` /
  `GymPowerUpsCombat` / `GymWeapons` scenes. No per-scene fork of the effect.
- [ ] **AC4 — Responsiveness preserved:** The gameplay effect (effect applied to
  the registry, lives/weapon updates, P4 bullet clear) and the pop SFX fire
  immediately on overlap, exactly as today. The absorb VFX is cosmetic only and
  does not delay the applied effect.
- [ ] **AC5 — Tests & suite green:** Unit/scene tests cover the absorb
  animation maths, the pop SFX, and collection in at least one path per scene;
  `npm test` passes.

## Constraints

- No new runtime dependencies; use the existing Web Audio synthesis helpers and
  Phaser `Graphics`/delta-time patterns.
- Tests must be deterministic: drive scenes through the existing game harness;
  never rely on the real render loop; audio is a safe no-op headless.
- Reuse existing modules — do not fork `PowerUp`, `EffectsRegistry`, `HUD`,
  `icons`, `audio`, `magnet` or the particle VFX.
- All written output in UK English.

## Existing state

- Drops are `Phaser.GameObjects.Graphics` positioned at `(x, y)` with a scale
  set each frame from `PowerUp.currentScale`; collection currently calls
  `drop.graphics.destroy()` on the same frame.
- `playPowerUpCollectSound()` (a two-tone ascending chime) already exists in
  `src/audio/effects.ts` and is the generic fallback in `PlayScene`,
  `GymFormationScene` and `GymPowerUpsCombat`. Type-specific cues already exist
  for P5 (`playSpeedBoostCollectSound`), P8 (`playExtraLifeCollectSound`) and P9
  (`playMagnetCollectSound`), plus weapon pickup cues.
- `src/powerups/magnet.ts` (`applyMagnetAttraction`) is an existing precedent
  for animating a drop's position toward the ship and syncing its `Graphics`.
- `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` is the precedent for a pure-logic VFX module
  plus a thin Phaser rendering entry point.
- Collection paths: `PlayScene._collectDrop`, `GymFormationScene._collectDrop`,
  `GymPowerUpsCombat._collectDrop`, `GymPowerUps._collectDrop`,
  `GymWeapons._collectDrop`.

## Desired change

1. **New pop SFX** — add `playPowerUpCollectPopSound()` (name indicative) to
   `src/audio/effects.ts`: a short percussive pop distinct from the existing
   chime; safe no-op without an `AudioContext`.
2. **Absorb animation helper** — add a shared module (for example
   `src/powerups/collectAnimation.ts`) exposing the pure state step (move toward
   the ship, shrink, morph/shear over a tunable duration) plus the scene-facing
   spawn/update API.
3. **Wire in** — every collection path starts the absorb animation instead of
   destroying the `Graphics` immediately, keeps the drop alive only for the
   animation duration, then destroys it. The gameplay effect and pop SFX are
   applied immediately on overlap.
4. **Docs** — note the new collection cue in the GDD audio section (§7.3) and
   the relevant scene documentation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Add `playPowerUpCollectPopSound()` (short percussive pop).
- `src/audio/effectsMaster.test.ts` (and/or `src/audio/effects.test.ts`) — Test the new pop cue exists and no-ops safely.
- `src/powerups/collectAnimation.ts` — New shared pure-logic absorb state step + thin Phaser entry point (target-position, scale, morph over a tunable duration).
- `src/powerups/collectAnimation.test.ts` — New unit tests for convergence, scale, morph and completion.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Start the absorb animation + play the pop on collection (replace the immediate `graphics.destroy()`).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — Extend collection tests for the absorb animation and pop cue.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Wire absorb + pop into the shared combat base (covers `GymEnemies`/`GymBoss`).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — Extend collection tests.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — Wire absorb + pop into the legacy gyms.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts` — Extend collection tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3: update the SFX event catalog "Power-up pickup" row (currently "Bright, ascending blip") and the player-audio notes to describe the new pop cue and absorb VFX.

## Related work

### Related work items

- **AH-0MU44M9NQ0006613** — Collect drops with effects and HUD (completed): the shared fly-over collection path and `EffectsRegistry` wiring this builds on.
- **AH-0MU3VOQKH005YOBH** — Spawn power-ups in all combat gym scenes (completed): the shared `GymFormationScene` power-up layer.
- **AH-0MTE8EBJR001F2L2** — Documentation: GDD section 6.4 architecture, code comments (completed): audio-cue documentation precedent.
- **AH-0MUAYB41U002GD8P** — The powerup status list overlaps the Lives count (open): unrelated HUD layout issue, surfaced by keyword overlap.

### Repository file matches

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — existing power-up spawn/despawn/collect cues and synthesis helpers.
- `src/powerups/magnet.ts` — existing precedent for animating drops toward the ship.
- `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` — precedent for a shared pure-logic VFX module.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 SFX event catalog: the "Power-up pickup" row currently reads "Bright, ascending blip"; it needs updating for the new pop cue, and the absorb VFX should be noted.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MT7VE4SX0005A8V** – Add a Magnet power up (completed)
- **AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F** – Asteroids as an enemy (completed)
- **AH-0MT99K3FE008CT13** – Create E4 Phaser gym scene (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: contexthub, feel, hell, item, need (+10 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: collected, feel, hell, item, need (+10 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: belongs, feel, hell, item, need (+9 more)

> Note: this automated report is keyword-driven and, because the original
> description contained migration boilerplate, it surfaced mostly unrelated
> items. The curated "Related work" section above is the authoritative list;
> the automated report is retained for traceability.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (scope):** "when a power up is collected" is taken to mean **all**
  collection paths (main game + all gym scenes) for consistency, implemented via
  one shared helper. If only the main game is wanted, the gym wiring can be
  dropped.
- **Assumption (timing):** the gameplay effect and pop SFX fire immediately on
  overlap (preserving current responsiveness); the absorb VFX is cosmetic and
  does not gate the effect. This keeps existing effect tests valid.
- **Assumption (SFX):** the new pop replaces the generic
  `playPowerUpCollectSound()` fallback. Existing type-specific cues
  (P5/P8/P9, weapon pickups) are retained — flagged in case the producer wants
  the pop to be the sole collection cue.
- **Assumption (VFX):** one generic absorb treatment for all types ("single type
  for now"), per the producer's answer.
- **Risk:** keeping the drop alive during the animation while the effect is
  already applied could double-apply or re-collect — mitigate by marking the
  drop as collected/absorbing and excluding it from the collect gate.
- **Risk:** the shared `GymFormationScene` change could regress `GymEnemies`/
  `GymBoss` — mitigate by wiring incrementally and running the full suite.
- **Risk (scope creep):** per-type VFX variants and a richer morph are
  attractive; recorded as future work rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (SFX):** The codebase already plays `playPowerUpCollectSound()` (a
  two-tone ascending chime) plus type-specific cues for P5/P8/P9. Does the
  existing chime satisfy "pop SFX", or is a different sound wanted?
  — **Answer (producer):** "different" — a new, genuinely "pop"-like sound.
- **Q2 (VFX):** What visual effect is wanted on collection?
  — **Answer (producer):** "is it possible to 'suck' it into the ship. That is
  morph its shape so that it looks like it is being sucked into the ship? If not
  then a flash/glow effect will suffice." **Feasibility confirmed** (see Problem
  / Desired change): implement the absorb/suck animation.
- **Q3 (differentiation):** Different VFX per type, or generic?
  — **Answer (producer):** "single type for now" — one generic effect.

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-09-22 01:03 UTC** — Plan skill run (auto-dispatched). Decomposed into 6 child work items across 4 vertical-slice phases; wired dependency edges (F3/F4/F5 ← F1+F2; F6 ← F3+F4+F5). All children set to `intake_complete`.
- **2026-09-22 01:11 UTC** — AC coverage review run; semantic coverage confirmed complete (parent ACs are high-level, children specific). Parent stage advanced to `plan_complete`.

## Plan: feature breakdown

| Phase | ID | Title | Depends on |
|-------|----|-------|------------|
| 1 Foundation | AH-0MUBYSNGU0051XVO | Pop SFX: playPowerUpCollectPopSound() with unit test | — |

# Power Ups scene title in index page

## Problem statement

The gym index derives each scene's display label by stripping the leading
`Gym` from the scene key (`src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts` → `displayLabelFromKey`).
`GymPowerUpsCombat` therefore reads **"PowerUpsCombat"**, but the threat-free
power-up gym `GymPowerUps` reads simply **"PowerUps"** — an ambiguous,
unclassified label next to its combat counterpart. Rename the scene so its
derived label becomes **"PowerUpsUtility"**.

## Users

- **Developer / play-tester** opening the dev gym index to pick a scene.
  - *As a developer, I want the threat-free power-up gym to be clearly labelled
    so I can distinguish it from the combat power-up gym at a glance.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Scene rename:** the non-combat power-up gym is renamed
  `GymPowerUps` → `GymPowerUpsUtility` across file, class and scene key:
  `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts`, `export class GymPowerUpsUtility`,
  `super({ key: 'GymPowerUpsUtility' })`. Its test file is renamed to match.
- [ ] **AC2 — Index label:** the gym index lists the scene with the label
  **"PowerUpsUtility"** (and still lists `PowerUpsCombat` unchanged), sorted
  alphabetically: `Boss, Player, PowerUpsCombat, PowerUpsUtility, Weapons`.
  Asserted in `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts`.
- [ ] **AC3 — No stale references:** no remaining occurrences of the bare
  identifier/key `GymPowerUps` (excluding `GymPowerUpsCombat`) in `src/`,
  `docs/`, or `README.md`.
- [ ] **AC4 — Behaviour unchanged:** spawning, lifecycle, collection, magnet,
  HUD and back-button behaviour of the scene are untouched (rename only); the
  scene-level test suite still passes.
- [ ] **AC5 — Documentation:** all related documentation is updated to reflect
  the changes, including code comments, `README.md`, and any relevant wiki or
  docs site entries (notably `docs/Game Design Document.md` and
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`).
- [ ] **AC6 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Rename only** — no functional/behavioural change to the scene.
- Follow the existing gym convention (`Gym<Name>.ts`, class and key `Gym<Name>`)
  so `import.meta.glob` auto-discovery and `sceneClassFromModule` continue to work.
- `GymPowerUpsCombat` must remain unchanged (label stays "PowerUpsCombat").
- Keep the index auto-discovery intact — do not hard-code labels in `GymIndex.ts`.

## Existing state

- `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts` — `displayLabelFromKey()` strips a leading `Gym`;
  discovery is directory-driven via `import.meta.glob`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.ts` — class `GymPowerUps`, key `'GymPowerUps'`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.test.ts` — 37 references to the old name.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` — expects labels `['Boss','Player','PowerUps','PowerUpsCombat','Weapons']`
  and keys including `'GymPowerUps'`.
- Comment/doc references in `src/core/constants.ts`, `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts`,
  `src/ui/HUD.ts`, `README.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`,
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.
- No runtime caller starts the scene by the literal key (the index auto-discovers it),
  so the rename is safe.

## Desired change

Rename the scene to `GymPowerUpsUtility` (file, class, scene key) and update the
matching test file plus all documentation/comment references. The gym index then
renders the label **"PowerUpsUtility"** via the existing derivation — no change to
`GymIndex.ts` or `gymDiscovery.ts` is required.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.ts` → `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` — rename file, class and scene key
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.test.ts` → `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.test.ts` — rename file and update all references
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` — update expected label (`PowerUpsUtility`) and key (`GymPowerUpsUtility`)
- `README.md` — rename the "GymPowerUps Gym Scene" section and path references
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — update the scene tree entry (key/label)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — update the scheme-aware routing reference
- `src/core/constants.ts`, `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts`, `src/ui/HUD.ts` — update code comments

## Related work

- **AH-0MUAYB2XR007N10W** – Player gym scene improvements (open) — sibling gym-index/label polish.
- **AH-0MTHG5JVP006U6K7** – Retire per-enemy gym scenes (completed) — prior gym-index restructuring.
- **AH-0MT7QQGBU008V4R0** – Write the Game Design Document (completed) — source of the scene-tree documentation.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the rename target is `GymPowerUpsUtility` (convention-consistent),
  producing label "PowerUpsUtility"; `GymPowerUpsCombat` is left untouched.
- **Risk:** a hard-coded `'GymPowerUps'` scene key would break at runtime — grep
  shows only tests, docs and comments reference it, so no runtime caller is affected.
- **Risk (low):** doc drift if any reference is missed — AC3 covers a repo-wide grep.
- **Scope-creep risk:** other gym scenes (e.g. "Weapons") may deserve clearer labels;
  record those as separate work items, not in this scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** What display label should the non-combat power-ups scene use in the gym index?
  (Options offered: "PowerUps (Basic)", "PowerUps (Simple)", "PowerUps (No Enemies)",
  "PowerUps (Threat-Free)".)
  — **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** "PowerUpsUtility — rename the GymPowerUps
  scene to achieve this." Source: work-item comment `AH-C0MUBU38ZM006722P` (recorded
  after producer reply). Related: AH-0MUAYB4EJ005CIYQ.
- **Q (agent assumption, not asked):** how is "PowerUpsUtility" realised given labels are
  auto-derived? — **Decision:** rename to `GymPowerUpsUtility` so `displayLabelFromKey`
  yields `PowerUpsUtility`, preserving the gym naming convention.
  Source: `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`.

# Intake Brief — Need juice when the player is destroyed (AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZY)

> **Status of this brief:** the operator was asked four clarifying questions
> (see Appendix) and replied "continue" without answering. Per the workflow's
> "do not block indefinitely" rule, this brief proceeds on **documented
> assumptions** (marked `[ASSUMPTION]` throughout). Open questions are retained
> in the Appendix for producer validation; the item is flagged
> `needsProducerReview` until they are resolved.

## Problem statement

When the player is destroyed the game currently plays a single particle burst
(`spawnExplosionParticles(...SHIP_COLOR, SHIP_SIZE...)`), the shared enemy
`playDestructionSound()`, and a 150% scale pulse, then immediately respawns or
ends the run. There is no camera shake, no player-specific death sound, and no
layered secondary feedback, so the most consequential event in the game feels
flat. The operator wants "lots of juice … screen shake, particle explosion, SFX
etc. Go wild!"

## Users

- **Player** — feels a weighty, unmistakable consequence when their ship is
  destroyed, distinct from ordinary enemy kills, reinforcing that a life was
  lost (or the run ended).
- **Developer / designer tuning feel** — can adjust shake intensity, sound
  layering, flash strength, and extra layers through exposed constants in one
  place without editing each death path.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, when my ship is destroyed I feel a strong impact: the
  camera shakes hard, a bright flash frames the screen, the explosion is
  visibly larger than an enemy's, and a distinct low "hull breach" boom plays
  instead of the generic enemy pop — so a life lost reads differently from a
  kill.
- As a **player**, the effect scales: losing my final life (game over) feels
  even heavier than a mid-run respawn, without becoming disorienting.
- As a **developer**, I can tune `PLAYER_DEATH_SHAKE_INTENSITY`,
  `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_ALPHA`, and the dedicated sound's amplitude in one
  constants module, and the behaviour is covered by unit tests so tuning does
  not silently regress.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Shared player-death juice helper exists:** A reusable helper
  (e.g. `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` or an extension of
  `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`) can be invoked from a scene with
  `(scene, x, y)` and composes the full effect (screen shake + particle burst +
  flash + any additional layers), returning/recording handles so scene teardown
  can destroy them. Both player-death paths use it:
  `PlayScene._loseLife()` (real run, lives/game-over) and
  `GymFormationScene._hitPlayer()` (combat gym, in-place respawn).
- [ ] **AC2 — Screen shake:** A scene-camera shake is triggered on player
  destruction with a configurable intensity and duration (suggested defaults:
  intensity ~0.008–0.02, duration ~250–400 ms, full 2D). Shake strength is a
  tunable constant in one module. Verified by unit test with a camera spy
  (`camera.shake` called with the configured intensity/duration).
- [ ] **AC3 — Dedicated player-death SFX:** A new `playPlayerDestructionSound()`
  in `src/audio/effects.ts`, distinct from the generic
  `playDestructionSound()` (suggested: heavier/lower multi-layer cue — impact
  thump + descending body + brief noise tail), exposed amplitude/length as
  constants. The player-death paths call it **exactly once**; existing
  `playDestructionSound()` calls on those paths are replaced (no double-play).
  Verified by unit test (call-count + no generic sound on player death).
- [ ] **AC4 — Extra juice layers (assumption-marked):** At least two additional
  layered effects beyond particles + shake + sound, each configurable and
  testable. Proposed set `[ASSUMPTION]`: (a) a brief full-screen white/cyan
  **flash** (alpha fades ~1 → 0 over ~120–200 ms) and (b) **debris shards** or
  an expanding **shockwave ring** that outlive the particle burst briefly. Each
  layer is individually toggleable via a constant so the producer can drop any
  they dislike without code surgery.
- [ ] **AC5 — Severity scaling & no behaviour change:** The effect is heavier
  for run-ending death (final life / game over) than for a mid-run respawn
  `[ASSUMPTION]`, via a `severity` parameter. Respawn position, invulnerability
  duration, blink, lives/score accounting, and shield-absorption behaviour are
  unchanged; no changes to hit detection.
- [ ] **AC6 — Teardown / no leaks:** All juice-owned GameObjects (flash
  overlay, debris, shockwave, particles) are tracked and destroyed on scene
  `SHUTDOWN`; stop→restart of a scene instance leaks nothing (mirrors the
  existing `playerExplosions` registry pattern).
- [ ] **AC7 — Testing/validation:** Unit tests cover: shake fired with
  configured params; dedicated sound called exactly once and generic sound not
  called on the player path; flash fades and is destroyed; debris/shockwave
  lifecycle; severity scaling; teardown leaks nothing. Existing player/scene
  suites still pass (update any assertions that assume the old single-burst
  behaviour).
- [ ] **AC8 — Documentation:** GDD §7.2 (and §7.3 audio if the new cue is
  listed) updated to describe the player-death juice; code comments on new
  constants/helpers; README updated if it documents audio/VFX behaviour.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes**
  (`npm test` = `vitest run`) and `npm run typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`).

## Constraints

- **Engine:** Phaser 4.2.1 + TypeScript 7, Vite, Vitest 4 (existing stack).
  Prefer Phaser `camera.shake()` for shake and Graphics/tween layers for the
  rest, consistent with the existing Graphics-particle approach in
  `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`.
- **Performance:** must not drop FPS on web; layers are short-lived and pooled
  or destroyed promptly; no per-frame allocation leaks.
- **Neon aesthetic:** consistent with GDD §7.1 palette; player effects centre
  on `SHIP_COLOR 0x00ffff`.
- **No behaviour change beyond VFX/audio:** respawn, invulnerability, lives,
  score, and shield logic untouched; no double audio.
- **Testability:** pure logic (intensity/duration/severity mapping) separated
  from Phaser rendering so it is unit-testable with fakes/spies.
- **No heavy new audio assets assumed:** sounds are synthesised with the
  Web Audio `blip`/oscillator helpers already in `src/audio/effects.ts`
  `[ASSUMPTION]` (no binary asset pipeline in this repo).

## Existing state

- **Player-death particle burst already exists** (shipped in
  AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V, v0.1.3): `spawnExplosionParticles(scene, x, y,
  SHIP_COLOR, SHIP_SIZE, { patterns: resolvePatterns('player'), registry })`,
  called from `PlayScene._spawnPlayerExplosion()` and
  `GymFormationScene._spawnPlayerExplosion()`.
- **Sound:** both player paths call the generic enemy cue
  `playDestructionSound()` (`src/audio/effects.ts:430`, a 0.28 s descending
  sawtooth blip at volume 0.3). No player-specific cue exists.
- **Scale pulse:** both paths tween the ship to `PLAYER_HIT_SCALE_PEAK` (1.5)
  over `PLAYER_HIT_SCALE_PULSE_DURATION/2` (0.2 s) and back.
- **No camera shake anywhere:** `grep` for `camera.shake` / `this.cameras`
  across `src/` returns nothing.
- **Two death paths:**
  - `PlayScene._hitPlayer() → _loseLife(explodeShip=true)` — costs a life,
    triggers `_finishRun(false)` at 0 lives, else `respawnInPlace()` +
    invulnerability blink.
  - `GymFormationScene._hitPlayer()` — combat gym: increments
    `playerHitCount`, plays sound + particles + scale pulse, `respawnInPlace()`,
    sets invulnerability/blink.
- Relevant constants live in `src/core/constants.ts`
  (`PLAYER_HIT_SCALE_PEAK=1.5`, `PLAYER_HIT_SCALE_PULSE_DURATION=0.4`,
  `PLAYER_RESPAWN_INVULNERABLE=1.5`, `COMBAT_HIT_BLINK_INTERVAL=0.1`).

## Desired change

1. Add a shared player-death juice composition helper (pure severity→params
   mapping + thin Phaser application) in `src/vfx/`.
2. Add tunable constants for shake intensity/duration, flash alpha/duration,
   debris/shockwave counts/lifetimes, and severity multipliers, in one module.
3. Add a dedicated `playPlayerDestructionSound()` (layered, heavier) to
   `src/audio/effects.ts`; replace the generic `playDestructionSound()` call on
   the two player-death paths only (enemy paths unchanged).
4. Trigger scene-camera shake on player destruction, scaled by severity.
5. Add the extra juice layers (flash + debris/shockwave) as individually
   toggleable, teardown-tracked GameObjects.
6. Wire both `PlayScene._loseLife()` and `GymFormationScene._hitPlayer()` to the
   helper; preserve all existing non-VFX behaviour.
7. Add/extend unit tests and update GDD §7.2/§7.3 + comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` — **new.** Composes shake + flash + debris/
  shockwave (+ delegates to existing particle helper); pure `resolveJuiceParams(severity)`
  mapping and teardown registry.
- `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` — **new.** Shake params, flash/debris
  lifecycle, severity scaling, teardown.
- `src/vfx/constants.ts` (or `src/core/constants.ts`) — new tunables:
  `PLAYER_DEATH_SHAKE_INTENSITY`, `PLAYER_DEATH_SHAKE_DURATION`,
  `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_ALPHA`, `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_DURATION_MS`, debris/
  shockwave counts, `PLAYER_DEATH_SEVERITY_*` multipliers.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — new `playPlayerDestructionSound()` (+ constants);
  leave `playDestructionSound()` untouched for enemies.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_loseLife()` / `_hitPlayer()` /
  `_spawnPlayerExplosion()` call the new helper with severity `'fatal'` vs
  `'respawn'`; SHUTDOWN teardown updates.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `_hitPlayer()` /
  `_spawnPlayerExplosion()` call the helper with `'respawn'` severity;
  SHUTDOWN teardown updates (`playerExplosions` registry pattern).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene*.test.ts`
  — update/extend hit-response assertions.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.2 particle/VFX and §7.3 audio notes.

## Related work

- **Immediate predecessor (completed):** Add particle-based explosion VFX for
  enemy and player deaths (AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V) — delivered the shared
  `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`, colour jitter, three pattern emitters, and
  wiring to all death paths. Its scope-creep guard explicitly deferred
  **screen-shake, sound redesign, debris physics, and trailing smoke** to
  "linked work items if desired" — this item is that follow-up.
- Respawn player in same spot (AH-0MU3VQ0JR009CSIN) — `respawnInPlace()`
  behaviour that must be preserved.
- Add player to each Enemy Gym scene (AH-0MTD0Z0Y7003T1NT) — gym player
  presence.
- One Tank changes colour (AH-0MTVYBL2L0085G6G) — sibling colour-per-entity
  work; coordinates on palette usage.
- GDD §7.1 colour palette, §7.2 particle effects, §7.3 audio cues.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — "go wild" is unbounded / subjective.** Mitigation: bound the scope
  to a named layer set (shake, dedicated SFX, flash, debris/shockwave), each
  individually toggleable via constants; exact intensities are tunable and
  locked by unit tests, with a manual feel pass.
- **Risk — unanswered operator questions mean the layer set is a guess.**
  Mitigation: all invented scope is marked `[ASSUMPTION]`; the item is flagged
  `needsProducerReview`; each layer can be dropped without rework.
- **Risk — screen shake can cause discomfort / motion sickness.** Mitigation:
  keep duration short (~250–400 ms) and intensity modest; consider respecting
  a future reduced-motion setting (not in scope here — record as linked work
  item if the producer wants it).
- **Risk — test churn on hit-response suites.** Mitigation: update assertions
  to cover the new helper call/seams; keep behaviour guarantees (respawn,
  lives, no double-audio) explicit in tests.
- **Risk — double audio regression.** Mitigation: dedicated AC + test that the
  player path plays the new sound exactly once and not the generic cue.
- **Assumption — sounds are synthesised** via existing Web Audio helpers (no
  new asset pipeline).
- **Assumption — severity scaling** ('fatal' heavier than 'respawn') is wanted;
  easily removed if not.
- **Assumption — both death paths** (real run + combat gym) should get the
  juice; if only the real run is wanted, the gym wiring can be dropped.
- **Scope-creep guard:** reduced-motion accessibility setting, screen-edge
  vignette, controller rumble/haptics, score-popup redesign, and full audio
  redesign are out of scope; file as linked work items if desired.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Particle explosions already exist (completed in AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V). Do
  you want these enhanced (more particles, longer duration, additional effects
  layered on top), or is the particle part considered done?" — Operator replied
  "continue" without an answer. **OPEN QUESTION.** Working assumption: the
  existing particle burst stays as the base layer; *additional* layered effects
  (flash, debris/shockwave) are added on top.
- Q2: "Screen shake — none exists today. Intensity and duration? Single strong
  shake fading over ~200–300 ms, layered, or horizontal only vs full 2D?" —
  Operator replied "continue" without an answer. **OPEN QUESTION.** Working
  assumption: single full-2D shake, intensity ~0.008–0.02, duration ~250–400 ms,
  scaled by severity.
- Q3: "SFX — should the player death have its own dedicated sound distinct from
  enemy destruction? Layered sounds or a single improved sound?" — Operator
  replied "continue" without an answer. **OPEN QUESTION.** Working assumption:
  dedicated layered `playPlayerDestructionSound()`, distinct from the generic
  enemy cue.
- Q4: "\"Lots of juice\" — beyond particles, screen shake, and SFX, what other
  juice do you envision? (e.g. screen flash, debris, slow-mo, UI feedback,
  score popup, camera zoom?)" — Operator replied "continue" without an answer.
  **OPEN QUESTION.** Working assumption: brief full-screen flash + debris
  shards/expanding shockwave ring; nothing else.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX** – Diver should rotate to face the player and dive towards them (completed)
- **AH-0MTVYBL2L0085G6G** – One Tank changes colour (completed)
- **AH-0MTHG5BSP006A81R** – Gym index discovers all enemy configs (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+313 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mtvybl2l0085g6g, ac3, ac4, ac5, acceptance (+309 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mtvybl2l0085g6g, ac1, ac4, add, added (+246 more)

## Plan — feature decomposition (plan_complete)

**Decision:** Full planning. Effort is **Small** and risk **Medium**; the bundled
pre-check returned `decision: "plan"`. The plan-approval gate returned
`request_approval: false` (effort not Medium+, risk not High), so no approval pause was
taken — producer validation of the OPEN QUESTIONS below is still requested.

**Vertical-slice phasing:** every item is an end-to-end slice (module + tests + wiring +
docs where relevant); between phases the next item's description is re-checked. Test-first:
the pure parameter model (F1) is the test-first spec that fails before implementation, and
the cross-path verification sweep (F9) closes the loop after wiring.

### Features

| # | Feature | Type | Depends on | Effort | Risk | ID |
|---|---------|------|-----------|--------|------|----|
| F1 | Player-death juice parameter model and constants | task | — | S | Low | AH-0MUDY2GH3003NYY3 |
| F2 | Dedicated player-destruction SFX | task | — | S | Low | AH-0MUDY2ID7006VY3A |
| F3 | Screen shake and flash layers | task | F1 | M | Medium | AH-0MUDY2K1K005V5L5 |
| F4 | Debris shards and shockwave ring | task | F1 | M | Medium | AH-0MUDY2LRR0040035 |
| F5 | Compose spawnPlayerDeathJuice entry point | task | F1, F2, F3, F4 | M | Medium | AH-0MUDY2NE5008MLPJ |
| F6 | Wire shared CombatScene.applyPlayerHit | task | F5 | S | Medium | AH-0MUDY2P1J0032LC6 |
| F7 | Wire PlayScene lose-life path | task | F5 | S | Medium | AH-0MUDY2R4S009F0JI |

### Discovered scope correction

The intake brief lists **two** player-death paths (`PlayScene._loseLife()` and
`GymFormationScene._hitPlayer()`). Reading the code shows **three/four**:

- `CombatScene.applyPlayerHit()` — the shared base used by `GymEnemies` / `GymBoss` /
  `GymMinerals` via the default `onPlayerHit` (covered by F6).
- `PlayScene._loseLife()` — the real run, with `'fatal'` at 0 lives and `'respawn'`

`PlayScene.tryAbsorbPlayerHit()` (shield absorb) and `_loseLife(false)` (wave-timeout

- **OPEN QUESTION (to producer):** Should all three player-hit paths get the juice, or only
  the real run? Assumed all three.
- **OPEN QUESTION (to producer):** Is a reduced-motion / accessibility option expected? Out
  of scope per the intake scope-creep guard; file as a linked work item if wanted.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-09-23 — Plan skill decomposed AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZY into 10 child items (F1–F10),
  wired dependency edges, ran the six automated review stages and the AC-coverage review
  (proceed, 100%). Recorded the third player-hit path (`GymPowerUpsCombat`) as a
  discovered-scope correction and retained the intake OPEN QUESTIONS.

### Plan Appendix — questions & answers

# Symbols for weapons do not reflect what the weapon does

## Problem Statement

Weapon power-up icons in AI Hell do not reliably convey what each weapon does. The clearest example is the rapid-fire weapon (P2), whose sine-wave icon reads as a slow, undulating line rather than a high-rate stream of bullets — it should use **stacked dots** that are visibly closer together than the slower forward-firing cannon. The producer has asked that **all** weapon icons be revisited and redesigned where the symbol does not match the weapon's behaviour.

## Users

- **Player**: Needs to identify what each weapon power-up does at a glance during fast, bullet-dense gameplay.
- **Player**: Needs the icons to make relative fire rates distinguishable (cannon 400 ms vs rapid 125 ms) without reading HUD text.

## Example User Stories

- As a player, I want the rapid-fire icon to show tightly **stacked dots** so it reads as a fast stream of bullets, not a slow wavy line.
- As a player, I want every weapon icon to visually reflect that weapon's actual firing pattern and relative rate, so I can learn the system quickly.
- As a player, I want the icon to be recognisable on both the field drop and the HUD.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Rapid icon uses stacked dots.** The rapid-fire weapon icon is redesigned as a stack of discrete circular dots (no singular sine/waveform line); the dots are tightly spaced so the icon reads as a rapid stream of bullets.
2. **Fire-rate distinction.** The rapid icon (125 ms, yellow) reads as visibly denser/faster than the cannon icon (400 ms, cyan) — the rapid stack has more, tighter-spaced elements than the cannon's single-bullet representation — so both forward-firing weapons are distinguishable at a glance.
3. **All weapon icons revisited.** Cannon, Spread, Dual and Rapid (plus the Reset drop) are each reviewed against their actual fire pattern/rate; each revised icon reflects its weapon's behaviour, with a one-line rationale recorded in code comments.
4. **Style and API preserved.** Icons remain code-drawn neon outlines (no external art assets) in `src/powerups/icons.ts`, drawn through the existing `drawWeaponIcon` / `drawWeaponDrop` API and `WeaponDropIconId` type; the glowing drop bubble, colours, and HUD integration are unchanged.
5. **Tests and validation.** Unit tests in `src/powerups/icons.test.ts` assert the updated icon geometry (e.g. the rapid icon emits multiple dot draw commands and differs from the other weapon icons); full project test suite passes with the new changes.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — in particular the GDD §4.4 "Icon Suggestion" for P2 Rapid Fire ("Firing-rate waveform") and the icon-shape note in the GymWeapons implementation callout.

## Constraints

- **Code-first, no assets**: icons must be drawn with Phaser Graphics (GDD §7.1); no external images or fonts.
- **Neon aesthetic**: outlined shapes on black, matching existing `ICON_COLORS` / `WEAPON_ICON_COLORS`.
- **API stability**: `drawWeaponIcon` / `drawWeaponDrop` signatures and `WeaponDropIconId` must not change (used by field drops and HUD).
- **Scope**: the request covers **weapon** icons only (cannon/spread/dual/rapid/reset); non-weapon power-up icons (P3–P9) are out of scope.

## Existing State

`src/powerups/icons.ts` draws the weapon icons:

| Weapon | Colour | Icon (current) | Fire rate | Behaviour |
|--------|--------|----------------|-----------|-----------|
| Cannon | cyan | barrel line + bullet circle | 400 ms | single bullet straight ahead (permanent) |
| Spread | orange | three radial fan lines | 600 ms | 3-bullet fan (−30°/0°/+30°) |
| Dual | magenta | two parallel vertical bars | 500 ms | 2 parallel bullets (±8 px side offset) |
| Rapid | yellow | 4-cycle sine wave | 125 ms | single bullets at markedly higher rate |

The rapid icon's waveform metaphor does not read as "fast"; the producer has directed that it use **stacked dots**. Mixed metaphors across icons are explicitly acceptable (producer decision), so no single unified visual language is required — each icon should use the clearest metaphor for its weapon.

## Desired Change

- Redesign the **rapid** icon as tightly stacked dots.
- Re-review **cannon, spread, dual and reset** and adjust any icon whose symbol does not match its weapon's pattern/rate.
- Update the GDD §4.4 icon suggestion for P2 and the code comments in `src/powerups/icons.ts` to describe the new metaphors.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — Weapon icon drawing functions (`drawCannonIcon`, `drawSpreadIcon`, `drawDualIcon`, `drawRapidIcon`, `drawResetIcon`); primary change site.
- `src/powerups/icons.test.ts` — Geometry assertions for the redesigned icons.
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — Weapon catalogue (fire rates, patterns, bullet colours/sizes) — reference for matching icons to behaviour.
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — `PowerUpType` / `WeaponId` types.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — Standalone HUD; renders weapon icons (should need no change if the API is preserved).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 icon suggestion for P2 and GymWeapons icon-shape note.

## Related Work

- **Migrated from** ContextHub work item `WL-0MTPL7K9E0025BWB` (misfiled in ContextHub; belongs to AI_Hell).
- **AH-0MTE8EB6Q007EU0J** — *Icons: code-drawn icons for P3, P4, P6, P7* (completed): established the code-drawn icon approach in `src/powerups/icons.ts`.
- **AH-0MTG5MGPZ00986B4** — *Power ups need to be larger* (completed): added the glowing drop bubble and larger drop rendering; added the current `icons.test.ts` geometry tests.
- **AH-0MTCNZX16007ECPS** — *Power-up catalogue + effects (P5, P8, P9)* (completed): AC6 required code-drawn neon icons per GDD §4.4 shared by field drops and HUD.
- **AH-0MTCO0FYP008IR59** — *Standalone HUD class (attachable to any scene)* (completed): renders each active weapon's icon; relies on the preserved icon API.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Subjectivity**: icon clarity is partly subjective; "reflects the weapon" cannot be fully machine-verified. Mitigation: measurable proxies (dot count/spacing, geometric difference between icons) in unit tests.
- **Scope creep**: "revisit all symbols" could expand into a full visual redesign of every power-up. Mitigation: constrain to weapon icons (cannon/spread/dual/rapid/reset); record any non-weapon icon ideas as linked follow-up work items, not in this change.
- **Legibility at small sizes**: field drops and HUD rows render icons at different sizes; a dot stack must remain legible when small. Mitigation: test at the drop size and HUD size.
- **Assumption**: the existing `drawWeaponIcon` / `drawWeaponDrop` API is sufficient; no new icon types are needed.
- **Assumption**: mixed metaphors are acceptable (producer-confirmed), so no unification is required.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

1. **Scope — rapid icon only, or all icons?**
   - Q: Should we only fix the rapid-fire icon (the concrete example given), or does the producer want all four weapon icons reviewed and potentially redesigned?
   - **Answer (producer, interactive reply)**: "revist all" — revise all weapon icons.
2. **Rapid icon metaphor**
   - Q: Should the rapid icon use more wave cycles (higher frequency sine wave), a different visual metaphor entirely (e.g. stacked dots, speed lines), or both?
   - **Answer (producer, interactive reply)**: "stacked dots" — use a stacked-dots metaphor.
3. **Visual consistency across icons**
   - Q: Should all weapon icons use a single visual metaphor (e.g. all bullets, all abstract symbols), or is the current mixed-metaphor approach acceptable with only the rapid icon improved?
   - **Answer (producer, interactive reply)**: "mixed is OK" — mixed metaphors are acceptable; no unification required.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** – Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene (completed)
- **AH-0MUCST2HU0097BIG** – Test: Choice strategy distinctness and permanent effects (completed)
- **AH-0MTECNKPC00954HH** – Test: Per-scene — player/combat assertions + regression (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: abstract, ac6, active, added, adjust (+219 more)
- `README.md` — matched: acceptance, active, actual, added, adjust (+209 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: active, actual, added, api, art (+149 more)

---

## Intake brief

**Headline:** Add a shared `Help (?)` affordance to the three power-up/weapon gym scenes that pauses the gym and shows a code-drawn icon, name and one-line description for every drop that gym can spawn, with the copy sourced from the shared catalogues.

### Problem statement

The power-up and weapon gym scenes are the project's primary tuning and demonstration surfaces, but a player or developer arriving in a gym has no way to learn what each drop on the field actually does short of reading the GDD. The gyms need an in-context help overlay that pauses the gym and shows, for every drop that gym can spawn, the drop's icon, its name and a one-line description.

### Users and user stories

- **As a developer tuning a gym**, I want to press `?` (or click a `Help (?)` button) and see the icon + effect of every drop this gym can spawn, so I can interpret what I am observing without leaving the gym or opening the GDD.
- **As a player/investigator exploring the dev gym index**, I want the help to show the *same* icon I see on the field and an accurate one-line description, so I can recognise drops at a glance.
- **As a maintainer**, I want the help text to come from the shared catalogues so it can never drift from the implemented behaviour.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Each of `GymPowerUpsUtility`, `GymPowerUpsCombat` and `GymWeapons` renders a `Help (?)` text button immediately next to the existing `← INDEX` button, and pressing `?` opens the same help overlay. Opening the help **pauses** the gym's simulation (movement, spawning, firing all stop) and resumes exactly where it paused on close.
2. The help overlay lists exactly the drop types the current gym can spawn, one row per drop, each showing the code-drawn icon that matches the in-game drop, the display name and a one-line description:
   - `GymPowerUpsUtility`: P5 Speed Boost, P8 Extra Life, P9 Magnet.
   - `GymPowerUpsCombat`: P3 Shield, P4 Bomb, P6 Phase Shift, P7 Teleport.
   - `GymWeapons`: Cannon (permanent default), Spread, Dual, Rapid, Reset.
3. Help descriptions are sourced from the shared gameplay catalogues — a `description` field on `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` (`src/powerups/types.ts`) and on the weapon catalogue plus a Reset entry (`src/utils/weapons.ts`) — so the help cannot drift from implemented behaviour; every catalogue entry exposes a non-empty `description`.
4. Closing the help via `?`, the overlay's `Close` control, or **ESC** resumes the gym. While the help overlay is open, **ESC closes the help and does not exit to the main menu**; once closed, ESC again returns to the main menu as it does today. The `Close` control is focused by default and operable by keyboard (Tab / arrow keys + Enter / Space).
5. The `Help (?)` button is placed adjacent to the existing `← INDEX` button without overlapping it, and the overlay is an opaque full-screen replacement (consistent with `PauseScene`) that is legible at the game's fixed 16:9 resolution.
6. Automated tests cover the shared helper, the `HelpScene`, and its integration into all three gyms (open pauses; content matches the gym's drop pool; `?`/`Close`/ESC resume; ESC does not reach the menu while open). **The full project test suite passes with the new changes.**
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (GDD §4.4 catalogue table and §6.4 gym sections).

### Constraints

- **No external art assets** — icons must reuse the existing code-drawn drawers `drawPowerUpIcon` / `drawWeaponIcon` (`src/powerups/icons.ts`), per the GDD §7.1 code-first convention.
- **The new `HelpScene` must not live in `src/scenes/gym/`**: gym scenes are auto-discovered by `import.meta.glob('../scenes/gym/*.ts')`, so a file placed there would appear as a bogus entry in the gym index. It belongs in `src/scenes/` and must be registered in `src/core/gameConfig.ts`.
- **Do not change existing navigation semantics**: the `← INDEX` button must still return to `GymIndex`, and ESC must still return to the main menu when help is closed.
- **Paused scenes do not receive keyboard input** (`KeyboardPlugin.isActive()` is false while paused), so the `?`/ESC *close* handling must live in `HelpScene`, not in the paused gym.
- The overlay is a dev/gym affordance; the shipped `PlayScene` is out of scope.

### Existing state

- The three gyms each call `addBackToIndexButton(this)` and `addBackToMenuOnEsc(this)` (`src/utils/gymNavigation.ts`); there is no help button, no `?` handling, and no help/legend screen anywhere in the game.
- `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` (`src/powerups/types.ts`) holds P3–P9 with `id`, `name`, `type`, optional `duration`/`maxStacks`, but **no description**. `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` (`src/utils/weapons.ts`) holds `cannon`/`spread`/`dual`/`rapid` with `id`, `name`, pattern data and **no description**; `reset` is a drop type with no catalogue entry.
- Each gym already owns an ordered list of the drops it spawns: `NON_COMBAT_ORDER` (`P5,P8,P9`), `COMBAT_ORDER` (`P3,P4,P6,P7`), `ROUND_ROBIN_ORDER` (`spread,dual,rapid,reset`).
- `PauseScene` (`src/scenes/PauseScene.ts`) is the precedent for a full-screen overlay that pauses gameplay and uses `FocusManager` for keyboard-operable controls; it is registered in `gameConfig.ts`.

### Desired change

1. Add a `description` string to every `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` entry and every `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` entry, plus a description for the `reset` drop (e.g. a small typed map/entry alongside the weapon catalogue), derived from GDD §4.4. Proposed one-line copy:
   - P3 Shield — "Absorbs one hit; a bubble protects the ship for 15 s."
   - P4 Bomb — "Instantly clears every on-screen enemy bullet (no enemy damage)."
   - P5 Speed Boost — "+50% movement speed for 10 s."
   - P6 Phase Shift — "3 s of intangibility — pass through enemies and bullets."
   - P7 Teleport — "Stores a use; press S or ↓ to warp to the nearest safe spot and gain 3 s Phase Shift on arrival."
   - P8 Extra Life — "+1 life immediately (starts at 3, capped at 5)."
   - P9 Magnet — "Permanently pulls nearby drops toward the ship (stacks up to 5)."
   - Cannon — "Permanent default weapon — one bullet straight ahead."
   - Spread — "Adds a 3-bullet fan (−30°/0°/+30°) for 10 s."
   - Dual — "Adds two side-by-side bullets for 10 s."
   - Rapid — "Adds single bullets at a much higher fire rate for 10 s."
   - Reset — "Clears all timed weapons, leaving only the Cannon."
2. Add a shared gym help helper (proposed `src/utils/gymHelp.ts`) exposing `addHelpButton(scene, { gymKey, drops })`, where `drops` is the gym's ordered drop list (`DropId | 'cannon'`). It renders the `Help (?)` button next to `← INDEX`, and on pointerdown or `?` keydown calls `scene.scene.pause()` then `scene.scene.launch('HelpScene', { gymKey, drops })`. It also exposes the id → `{ name, description, drawIcon }` lookup used by both the button and the overlay so icons/names/descriptions have one source.
3. Add `src/scenes/HelpScene.ts`: an opaque full-screen overlay titled with the gym label, rendering one row per requested drop (code-drawn icon + name + wrapped description), plus a focused `Close` control. It handles `?`, ESC and the `Close` control by `scene.stop()`-ing itself and `scene.resume(gymKey)`-ing the originating gym. Register it in `src/core/gameConfig.ts`.
4. Wire `addHelpButton` into the three gyms, passing each gym's existing drop-order constant (and `['cannon', ...ROUND_ROBIN_ORDER]` for `GymWeapons`).
5. Update the GDD §4.4/§6.4 and README gym sections, and add code comments documenting the overlay and the new catalogue description fields.

### Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/types.ts` — Add a `description` field to `PowerUpEntry` and a one-line description to every P3–P9 catalogue entry.
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — Add a `description` field to `WeaponDefinition` and descriptions for cannon/spread/dual/rapid; add a `reset` description entry.
- `src/utils/gymHelp.ts` — **New.** `addHelpButton(scene, config)`, the `HelpDropId` type and the id → `{ name, description, drawIcon }` lookup shared by the button and overlay.
- `src/scenes/HelpScene.ts` — **New.** Full-screen opaque help overlay scene (icon + name + description rows, focused `Close`, `?`/ESC handling, resume-gym lifecycle).
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` — Register `HelpScene` so it can be launched from the dynamically-added gym scenes.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` — Call `addHelpButton` with `NON_COMBAT_ORDER`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — Call `addHelpButton` with `COMBAT_ORDER`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — Call `addHelpButton` with the cannon + `ROUND_ROBIN_ORDER` drop list.
- `src/utils/gymHelp.test.ts` — **New.** Unit tests for the lookup/description coverage and button wiring.
- `src/scenes/HelpScene.test.ts` — **New.** Scene-level tests (open pauses; content per gym; `?`/`Close`/ESC resume; ESC does not reach the menu while open).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.test.ts`, `GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts`, `GymWeapons.test.ts` — Extend with help-button/overlay integration assertions.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Document the gym help overlay and the catalogue `description` fields (§4.4 / §6.4).
- `README.md` — Document the `Help (?)` affordance in the gym sections.

### Risks and assumptions

- **Input routing risk (mitigated by design):** a paused Phaser scene does not receive keyboard events, so the `?`/ESC *close* handling must live in `HelpScene`; if it were left on the gym the overlay could not be dismissed by keyboard. Tests must assert resume-on-close.
- **Discovery risk (mitigated by constraint):** placing `HelpScene` in `src/scenes/gym/` would leak it into the gym index; the brief pins it to `src/scenes/` + `gameConfig.ts` registration.
- **Drift risk (mitigated by AC3):** descriptions are read from the catalogues rather than duplicated in the overlay, so a future balance change to a drop's effect forces the help text to change in one place.
- **Copy-review risk:** the proposed one-line descriptions are derived from GDD §4.4; if the producer prefers shorter/rewritten copy, only the catalogue `description` strings need editing (no structural change).
- **Scope-creep risk:** extending the help to the full-pool combat formation gyms (`GymEnemies`/`GymBoss`) and to the shipped `PlayScene` is deliberately **out of scope** for this item. If desired, record these as separate follow-up work items (`discovered-from:AH-0MUAYB67I002REOZ`) rather than growing this one. The shared helper is deliberately gym-agnostic so those follow-ups are cheap.
- **Assumption:** the dev gym index (and therefore the gyms) is only reachable in dev mode, so the overlay is a developer/QA affordance and needs no persistence or localisation.

### Related work

- **Gym index scene (AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ)** — introduces the `← INDEX` button and directory-dynamic gym discovery that the help entry point sits beside.
- **Add ESC handler to remaining direct gym scenes (AH-0MUA9BBFV004Y1T0)** — establishes the ESC-to-menu behaviour the help overlay must not break while open.
- **Create gym scene for power-ups with spawning, collection, and standalone HUD (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT)** — the `GymPowerUpsUtility` gym whose drops the help documents.
- **Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene (AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR)** — the `GymWeapons` gym and the weapon/reset drop set.
- **Create combat gym scene for combat-coupled power-ups (AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40)** — the `GymPowerUpsCombat` gym and the P3/P4/P6/P7 drop set.
- **Power-up catalogue + effects (P5, P8, P9) (AH-0MTCNZX16007ECPS)** and **Catalogue extension: P3, P4, P6, P7 entries (AH-0MTE8EB36003YF0S)** — the catalogues that gain the `description` field.
- **In-game menu (AH-0MU9LPZ0G0015292)** — the `PauseScene` + `FocusManager` overlay pattern the help overlay should mirror.
- **Docs: GymPowerUps scene + ui/HUD.ts in GDD & README (AH-0MTCO0R4D0043TDL)** — the documentation surfaces to update.

### Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 (scope of gym scenes).** Which scenes get the help overlay? — **Answer (Producer, interactive reply):** **A** — shared, gym-agnostic helper + `HelpScene`, wired into the three named gyms only (`GymPowerUpsUtility`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymWeapons`). Source: interactive reply to the intake agent, 2026-09-23.
- **Q2 (open/close and pause semantics).** How does help open/close and what does ESC do while it is open? — **Answer (Producer):** **A** — `?` or the `Help (?)` button opens and pauses the gym; `?` / `Close` / ESC closes and resumes; while help is open ESC closes help first and never exits to the menu. Source: interactive reply to the intake agent, 2026-09-23.
- **Q3 (content source of truth and entries).** Where do descriptions live and what does each list include? — **Answer (Producer):** **A** — add a `description` field to `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` and the weapon catalogue (plus a reset entry), render help from the catalogues; `GymWeapons` lists Spread/Dual/Rapid/Reset plus the permanent Cannon. Source: interactive reply to the intake agent, 2026-09-23.

# Intake Brief — Asteroids drop collectable minerals that fill the ship's hold and grant a power-up choice

## Problem statement

Destroying a small asteroid currently only awards score and (for large/medium rocks) splits them; it never yields a collectable resource. We want destroyed small asteroids to leave behind **minerals** — small gold dots — that are collected by flying into them (by the player ship or by a non-asteroid enemy). Player collection fills a **ship's hold** (mineral store); when the hold is full the game pauses and offers **three power-ups**, one of which the player keeps **permanently for the run** (until death). Enemy collection builds a per-enemy mineral count that is partly spilled back as fresh minerals when that enemy is destroyed.

## Users

**Primary user — the player** during a PlayScene run (and in the new asteroids-only gym).

- *As a player, I want destroyed asteroids to drop collectable minerals, so that clearing rocks feels rewarding and feeds a progression loop.*
- *As a player, I want a visible hold counter, so that I know how close I am to my next reward.*
- *As a player, when my hold is full, I want to choose one of three power-ups to keep for the rest of the run, so that mineral gathering compounds into a build.*
- *As a player, I want enemies to be able to steal minerals and spill them on death, so that mineral gathering is contested and tactical.*

**Secondary users — developers/QA** validating the mechanic in the gym index.

- *As a developer, I want an asteroids-only mineral gym, so that I can observe drop/collect/re-drop and the hold-full choice in isolation.*
- *As a developer, I want the mechanic tunable through the game-rules config, so that balance can be adjusted without code changes.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Mineral drop on small-asteroid destruction.** Destroying a `small` asteroid spawns one or more **mineral** drops (small gold dots) at the destruction site; `large`/`medium` destructions do not themselves spawn minerals (their split children, once `small`, do). Minerals are **not** hit by bullets and cause **no damage or collision response** on contact with the player or an enemy.
- **AC2 — Player collection fills the hold.** Flying the player ship into a mineral removes it and increases the ship's mineral store by the configured collection amount (default **1**), up to the configured capacity (default **20**); the store is shown on the HUD (e.g. `Minerals: n/20`).
- **AC3 — Enemy collection and re-drop.** Every **non-asteroid** enemy that overlaps a mineral absorbs it (mineral removed, no damage) and increments that enemy's tracked mineral count; when that enemy is destroyed, **25–50 %** (configurable) of its collected count is re-spawned as individual mineral drops scattered at the explosion site.
- **AC4 — Hold-full power-up choice.** When the mineral store reaches capacity, the game pauses and a modal overlay presents **three distinct** power-up options; selecting one applies it to the player as a **permanent effect for the current run** (including weapon drops, which do not expire as they normally do), resumes play, and **resets the store to 0 carrying any overflow** (store = collected − capacity).
- **AC5 — Pluggable selection strategy.** The three offered options come from a pluggable strategy interface; the default implementation is a **random selection across the full existing drop pool (P3–P9 plus weapon drops)**, drawing distinct entries. Swapping the strategy requires no change to the choice scene or PlayScene wiring.
- **AC6 — Tunability.** Collection amount (default 1), hold capacity (default 20), and the re-drop fraction range (default 25–50 %) are read from the game-rules config (`src/core/rules.ts`) with sensible defaults and corrupt-config fallback, matching the existing rules pattern.
- **AC7 — Asteroids-only mineral gym.** A new gym scene (asteroids only) is registered in the gym index and demonstrates: small-asteroid mineral drops, player hold fill, HUD counter, enemy collection, re-drop on enemy death, and the hold-full choice overlay. Existing gym scenes spawn **100 random mineral drops on initialisation**.
- **AC8 — Testing/validation.** The mechanic is covered by meaningful automated tests (mineral lifecycle/collection rules, enemy count + re-drop distribution bounds, hold overflow arithmetic, choice-strategy distinctness and permanence, scene wiring) with coverage reported; the full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- **AC9 — Documentation.** GDD (§4.4/§4.5/§6.4 as appropriate) and README are updated to describe minerals, the hold, enemy collection/re-drop, the choice overlay and the new gym; code comments added on new modules.
- **AC10 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing drop infrastructure where sensible (the `PowerUp` grow/hold/shrink lifecycle, `EffectsRegistry`, spawner/placement modules, `HUD`, `icons`, audio cues) rather than forking it.
- All new numeric values default to the operator-stated values (collection **1**, capacity **20**, re-drop **25–50 %**) and are configurable via `src/core/rules.ts` with corrupt-JSON fallback, mirroring the existing pattern.
- The choice overlay must pause gameplay at the SceneManager level (mirroring `PauseScene`) so no further collection/damage occurs while choosing.
- Permanence is scoped to the run: chosen power-ups and the mineral store reset on death/restart (they do **not** persist across `GameState.startGame()` or into the leaderboard).
- UK English throughout; do not edit `.pi/`, `skill/`, or agent-infrastructure directories.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Asteroid.ts` — three tiers (`large`/`medium`/`small`); large/medium split into two smaller rocks; small destroys cleanly; 1 HP; never fires; `PlayScene._splitAsteroid` registers children with `WaveManager`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_onEnemyKilled` awards score and rolls a power-up drop (`_maybeDropPowerUp`, ~15–20 %); drops are only collectable by the player; `_hitPlayer` handles shield absorb / life loss.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — common enemy container with `destroySelf()`/`destroy()`; no per-enemy resource state today.
- `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts` — grow→hold→shrink→despawn lifecycle, >3 % collection gate; `spawner.ts` has `RoundRobinSpawner`/`WeightedRandomSpawner`; `placement.ts` avoids overlaps.
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — P3–P9 plus weapon drops (spread/dual/rapid/reset); `effects.ts` holds the `EffectsRegistry` (timed P3/P5/P6, instant P4, stacking P7/P9, permanent-life P8, timed weapons).
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — run state (`lives`, `score`, `level`, `bossDefeated`, `gameState`) with `startGame()` reset; the natural home for a mineral store.
- `src/core/rules.ts` — persisted game-rules config (spawn interval + drop weights) with `loadRules()`/`saveRules()`; the pattern to follow for new tunables.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — standalone HUD rendering lives and one row per active effect/weapon.
- `src/scenes/PauseScene.ts` — the existing modal-overlay pattern (SceneManager pause + launched scene).
- Gym framework: `src/scenes/gym/` (`GymPowerUps`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymWeapons`, `GymEnemies`, `GymBoss`, `GymPlayer`, `core/GymFormationScene`) with index auto-discovery (`src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts`, `GymIndex.ts`). There is **no** asteroids gym today.
- No mineral/cargo/hold concept exists anywhere in the codebase or worklog.

## Desired change

1. **New `Mineral` collectable** — small gold dot, no bullet interaction, no damage; collected on overlap by player or a non-asteroid enemy; persists until collected.
2. **Small asteroids drop minerals** — spawned at the destruction site in `PlayScene._onEnemyKilled` when `getSizeTier() === 'small'`.
3. **Per-enemy mineral count** — `BaseEnemy` tracks collected minerals; all non-asteroid types absorb overlapping minerals; on destruction 25–50 % of the count is re-spawned as individual dots at the explosion site.
4. **Ship's hold** — `GameState` gains a mineral store + capacity; HUD shows the counter; player overlap adds the configured amount.
5. **Hold-full choice** — a paused modal overlay offers three distinct power-ups; the chosen effect is permanent for the run; the store resets with overflow carried.
6. **Pluggable choice strategy** — an interface with a default random-across-all-drops implementation.
7. **Config tunables** — collection amount, capacity, re-drop fraction range in `rules.ts`.
8. **Asteroids-only mineral gym** — new gym scene + index registration; existing gyms pre-seed 100 random minerals on init.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/entities/Mineral.ts` — **New.** Gold-dot collectable: visual, spawn-at, player/enemy overlap semantics, no bullet/damage behaviour.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — Per-enemy mineral count, `collectMineral()`, and a re-drop count/position helper called on destruction.
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — Mineral store, capacity, `addMinerals()`/overflow arithmetic, reset on `startGame()`.
- `src/core/rules.ts` — New tunables: `mineralCollectAmount`, `mineralHoldCapacity`, `mineralRedropMin`/`mineralRedropMax` (+ defaults/merge).
- `src/core/constants.ts` — Mineral visual/size/depth constants (canonical values).
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — **New.** Pluggable `PowerUpChoiceStrategy` interface + default random-across-all-drops implementation.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — Support marking a chosen effect permanent for the run (no timer decrement / never expires).
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — Permanent weapon equipping (a chosen weapon does not time out).
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — **New.** Paused modal overlay offering three picks (mirrors `PauseScene` navigation).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Wire mineral spawn on small-asteroid kill, player/enemy overlap collection, re-drop on enemy death, hold-full → launch choice, store reset/overflow.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts` — **New.** Asteroids-only gym demonstrating the full mechanic.
- `src/scenes/gym/` (existing scenes / `core/GymFormationScene.ts`) — Seed 100 random mineral drops on init.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — Mineral store row (`Minerals: n/20`).
- `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts` / `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` — Register the new gym scene.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` / `README.md` — Document the mechanic and gym.

## Related work

- **AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F** — *Asteroids as an enemy* (parent of the asteroid implementation; mineral drops extend its destruction flow).
- **AH-0MU44M9NQ0006613** — *Collect drops with effects and HUD* (the drop-collection + HUD pattern to reuse).
- **AH-0MTCNZPHN003C5E1** — *Power-up core lifecycle + tunable constants* (the `PowerUp` lifecycle to reuse).
- **AH-0MTCNZX16007ECPS** — *Power-up catalogue + effects (P5, P8, P9)* (the effect registry the permanent choice builds on).
- **AH-0MU9LPZ0G0015292** — *In-game menu* (the `PauseScene` overlay pattern to mirror for the choice modal).
- **AH-0MTVYCM2N002NKE4** — *Player pickup pickups as soon as they touch* (pickup-on-contact semantics).
- **AH-0MUAYB3OU0087H9W** — *Collected powerups need some feel* (related collection feedback/juice).
- **AH-0MTCPL9NA0025ZUI** — *In-Game spawning should not be round robin* (weighted drop pool used by the default choice strategy).
- **AH-0MU6VSKZT006HBTR** — *Leaderboard: game-over score entry and localStorage display* (run-scoped state reset interaction).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** mineral-based progression could expand into trading/upgrades/economy. This brief is limited to drop → collect → hold → one permanent power-up choice; further economy ideas should become linked work items, not scope here.
- **Assumption:** minerals are stationary (no drift/despawn) and persist until collected; no lifetime is specified. If drift/lifetime is desired it will be added as a tunable.
- **Assumption:** the one mineral per small-asteroid destruction count is configurable via a drop-amount tunable (default 1) rather than a random range.
- **Assumption:** "permanent until death" means the chosen effect persists for the run and resets with the rest of `GameState`; it is not written to the leaderboard.
- **Assumption:** the three offered options are guaranteed distinct; if the pool cannot supply three distinct entries it degrades gracefully (fewer options).
- **Risk:** pausing for the choice mid-wave could interact with wave timers/invulnerability timers; the overlay must use SceneManager pause (as `PauseScene` does) so all timers freeze consistently.
- **Risk:** making selected weapons permanent touches `Player`/`EffectsRegistry` semantics that the existing `WeaponEffect` timer model assumes; tests must lock the "chosen weapon never expires" behaviour.

## Open Questions

None outstanding — all three interview rounds answered (see Appendix).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Round 1**

- **Q1: What should happen when an enemy touches a mineral?** — Answer (operator, interactive reply): Keep a **count** of how many minerals the enemy has collected; when the enemy is destroyed, **25–50 %** of them are left behind by the explosion (as individual drops).
- **Q2: Which asteroid tiers drop minerals, and how many?** — Answer (operator, interactive reply): **Small asteroids only**.
- **Q3: Where do the three offered power-ups come from?** — Answer (operator, interactive reply): Make the selection process **pluggable**, starting with a **random selection across all power-ups (including weapons)**.

**Round 2**

- **Q4: Enemy collection scope and re-drop shape?** — Answer (operator, interactive reply): **All enemy types except asteroids** collect; the re-drop is **individual dots**; (asteroids are excluded from collecting, so split-child inheritance does not apply).
- **Q5: Choice presentation, hold reset, permanence?** — Answer (operator, interactive reply): (a) the game **pauses** with a modal overlay; (b) the hold **resets to 0 with overflow held**; (c) the chosen power-up is **permanent for the run even if normally timed**, and the three options are distinct.
- **Q6: Scope and tunability?** — Answer (operator, interactive reply): a **new asteroids-only gym scene**; **existing gym scenes should have 100 random mineral drops when initialised**; the tunable-via-`rules.ts` and HUD-counter assumptions were **confirmed**.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTECNI1Y001O2OV** – Test: Core scene — enemy live aim tracking (completed)
- **AH-0MTVYBL2L0085G6G** – One Tank changes colour (completed)
- **AH-0MU7305Z2003NII3** – Implement PlayScene — wave management integration (completed)

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: asteroid, asteroids, bullets, choice, collect (+55 more)
- `README.md` — matched: asteroid, asteroids, bullets, collect, collection (+49 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: asteroid, asteroids, bullets, collect, collection (+38 more)

# Pop SFX: playPowerUpCollectPopSound()

## Headline
Add a short percussive pop sound to src/audio/effects.ts, distinct from the existing two-tone ascending chime (playPowerUpCollectSound()). It is played whenever a power-up drop is collected.

## Problem statement
Power-up collection currently uses playPowerUpCollectSound() -- a cheerful two-tone ascending chime. The producer wants a genuinely pop-like sound that is audibly distinct from this chime.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 -- Sound design: playPowerUpCollectPopSound() is a short (<= 100 ms) percussive pop, synthetically distinct from playPowerUpCollectSound(). The wave type and frequency contour must be clearly different.
- AC2 -- Safe no-op: Without an AudioContext (headless tests), the function degrades to a safe no-op -- no throw.
- AC3 -- Unit test: A test in src/audio/effects.test.ts asserts the function exists, is callable, and that it produces the expected synthesis parameters (wave type, frequency contour, duration, volume <= 0.2) against a mock AudioContext.
- AC4 -- Distinct from other cues: The pop is distinguishable from the collection chime and all other audio cues by wave type or frequency contour.

## Key Files

- src/audio/effects.ts -- Add playPowerUpCollectPopSound() function.
- src/audio/effects.test.ts -- Add unit test for the pop cue (mock + no-op paths).

# Absorb Animation Module: shared collectAnimation.ts with unit tests

## Headline
Create a new shared module src/powerups/collectAnimation.ts that exposes:
1. A pure-logic state-stepper function (move drop position toward ship, shrink scale, morph/shear over a tunable duration)
2. A thin Phaser-facing entry point (spawn an animation on a Graphics object, update it per frame, destroy on completion)

## Problem statement
On collection, drops currently have their Graphics destroyed immediately. We need a reusable animation that makes drops visually suck into the ship -- position converges on the ship, scale shrinks to zero, and the shape/shear morphs during the animation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 -- Pure state stepper: stepCollectAnimation(state, shipX, shipY, dt) advances position toward the ship using linear interpolation (lerp), shrinks scale toward 0, and applies a shear/morph rotation. All inputs and outputs are plain objects -- no Phaser types.
- AC2 -- Tunable parameters: The animation has a configurable duration (default target <= 0.3 s), speed constant, and the step function is deterministic given the same inputs.
- AC3 -- Phaser entry point: spawnCollectAnimation(graphics, dropX, dropY, shipX, shipY, duration) creates and returns a handle with update(dt), isComplete(), and destroy() methods. The Graphics object is destroyed on completion.
- AC4 -- Morph/shear: During animation, the drop shape is morphed (shear/rotation) to evoke the impression of being sucked/elongated toward the ship. This is a single generic treatment for all drop types.
- AC5 -- Unit tests: Tests cover position convergence, scale shrink, shear progression, completion detection, and safe no-op when Graphics is null.
- AC6 -- Reuse pattern: The module mirrors the architecture of src/powerups/magnet.ts (pure logic + scene seam) and src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts (pure state + thin Phaser entry point).

## Key Files

- src/powerups/collectAnimation.ts -- New file: pure step function + Phaser entry point.
- src/powerups/collectAnimation.test.ts -- New test file: convergence, scale, morph, completion.

# PlayScene: wire absorb animation + pop SFX into collection path

## Headline
Wire the new pop SFX and absorb animation into PlayScene._collectDrop so that collection provides immediate tactile feedback.

## Problem statement
PlayScene._collectDrop currently: applies the effect, destroys the drop's Graphics immediately, then plays the pickup cue. We need to replace the immediate destroy with starting the absorb animation and playing the pop SFX.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 -- Gameplay effect fires immediately: The effect (registry apply, lives update, P4 bullet clear) fires on the same frame as overlap, exactly as today.
- AC2 -- Pop SFX plays immediately: playPowerUpCollectPopSound() is called on collection alongside the existing per-type pickup cue.
- AC3 -- Absorb animation starts: spawnCollectAnimation() is called with the drop's current position and the ship's world position. The drop's Graphics stays alive and is updated each frame by the animation.
- AC4 -- Drop destroyed on animation complete: When the absorb animation completes, the drop's Graphics is destroyed and the drop is removed from the active drops array.
- AC5 -- No double-apply: The drop is marked as absorbing so the overlap gate does not re-collect it during the animation.
- AC6 -- Unit test: Extend PlayScene tests to verify the absorb animation starts on collection, the pop SFX plays, and the drop is cleaned up after animation.

## Key Files

- src/scenes/PlayScene.ts -- Modify _collectDrop to start animation instead of destroy; add frame update for animation; add pop SFX call.
- src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts -- Extend collection tests for absorb animation and pop cue.

# Reusable in-canvas focus manager (AH-0MU9LKQEP008LCX9-C1)

## Summary

Create the reusable in-canvas focus manager that tracks focusable controls, cycles focus on Tab/arrow keys, activates on Enter/Space, renders a visible focus style, and cleans up on shutdown.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** Focus manager exposes `register(control, actionCallback)` and `unregister(control)` APIs.
- **AC2:** On registration, the first control is focused by default.
- **AC3:** Tab cycles forward through registered controls with wrap-around; Shift+Tab cycles backward.
- **AC4:** Arrow keys (up/down for vertical, left/right for horizontal — configurable) cycle focus with wrap-around.
- **AC5:** Enter and Space activate the focused control by invoking its action callback.
- **AC6:** The focused control receives a visible focus style (brighter colour + highlight border); unfocused controls restore their prior style.
- **AC7:** `shutdown()` removes all keyboard event listeners and clears the registry.
- **AC8:** Unit tests cover: default focus, Tab/Shift+Tab cycling (including wrap), arrow-key cycling (including wrap), Enter/Space activation, and shutdown cleanup.

## Key Files

- `src/utils/focusManager.ts` (new) — FocusManager class with register/unregister, keyboard handling, focus styling, shutdown.
- `src/utils/focusManager.test.ts` (new) — Unit tests for all ACs above.

## Dependencies

- None (core utility, implemented first)

## Test: Asteroid behaviour during the transition period (Phase 2)

**Related to:** AH-0MU8TWF1H007OG2L — Asteroids should not explode when time runs out, instead carry them over

**Goal:** Verify that carried-over asteroids keep moving, remain shootable, and can ram the player during the level/wave transition period, while non-asteroid enemy movement/fire stays suspended.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. During the transition (`transitionTimer > 0`), a carried-over asteroid continues to move (its position changes across ticks in line with its velocity).
2. During the transition, a player bullet overlapping a carried-over asteroid destroys it (`getAliveCount()` decreases and the asteroid's `alive` flag is false).
3. During the transition, player-asteroid overlap costs the player one life.
4. During the transition, non-asteroid enemy movement/fire remains suspended and enemy-bullet-vs-player collisions do not occur.
5. After the transition completes, normal gameplay resumes with any un-destroyed carried-over asteroids still present.

**Implementation approach:**
- Add `it()` cases in `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`
- Boot a play scene, force a wave timeout so an asteroid carries over into the transition, then tick through the transition:
  - Assert position/velocity continuity
  - Fire a player bullet at the asteroid during the transition and assert it is destroyed
  - Move the player onto the asteroid during the transition and assert a life is lost
  - Assert suspended enemy behaviour is unchanged

**Key Files:**
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — add new test cases

**Phase:** 2 of 3 (transition-period asteroid behaviour)

**Depends on:** Phase 1 implementation
